This chapter collects the Limits layers of the other chapters in one place, grouped by severity. It states no limit that its source section does not state, and where a section and the outline disagree, the section is followed. There are 144 items from 13 chapters, 6 more from the conservation chapter that is not in the book yet, and three placeholders for limits that a pending code change alters.

Each item names the section it comes from and the evidence that section gives: a code location at chengcli/snapy `e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` (symbol and `file:lines`), a registered test, an executable check with its check line, or an issue. The links to the code are in the source sections; "stated in the section" marks an item whose section states it from the code without a narrower citation. Two kinds of statement are not repeated here: the remark, made in most Limits layers, that untested switch combinations are listed in the switch coverage matrix (@sec-ch12-matrix), which is one item below, and statements about what an author did or did not run for a draft, which describe the evidence of a chapter, not a limit of the code.

Three classes are used:

- **Wrong results possible** (@sec-ch16-wrong): a configuration the code accepts can produce wrong results, or conservation that does not hold, without an error.
- **Restricted applicability** (@sec-ch16-restricted): a scheme, switch or path is limited to some configurations, or a combination is untested, so results outside them are not established.
- **Performance and usability** (@sec-ch16-usability): cost, diagnostics, documentation or defaults that surprise a user, with no effect on the results of a correct configuration.

## Wrong results possible {#sec-ch16-wrong}

Items where a configuration the code accepts can produce wrong results, or conservation that does not hold, without an error.

| limit | source | evidence |
|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------|---------------------------|
| A driver-split source applied after a `Mesh` call can leave previously exchanged ghosts stale before the next advance (inferred from call order, not measured). | @sec-ch01-mesh | `forward` (`mesh.cpp:331-365`) |
| Constant heat capacities are assumed even if the thermo card requests temperature-dependent options. | @sec-ch02-ideal-moist | `_cons2prim` (`ideal_moist.cpp:164-233`) |
| The temperature Newton iteration warns at its iteration limit and returns the current estimate; this is not the saturation-failure counter, so the step is not rejected. | @sec-ch02-moist-mixture | `_intEng_to_temp` (`kintera thermo_y.cpp:495-517`) |
| The checks that a block holds more cells than its ghost zone never fire (they read `nx1` before `repartition` sets it), so a block narrower than its ghost zone is not refused. | @sec-ch03-globalgrid | `coordinate.cpp:164-179` |
| Hypothesis read from the code, not measured: the $m_2$, $m_3$ angular-momentum terms multiply a radial-only factor by the full face area, carrying an extra solid-angle factor; no test checks these terms. | @sec-ch03-sphpolar | `forward` (`spherical_polar.cpp:224-310`) |
| Corners involving $x_1$ (blocks split in $x_1$ on `cubed`) are never exchanged or synthesised; at an internal $x_1$ seam they keep stale values, which a cross-derivative operator would read. | @sec-ch03-exchange | `fill_corners` (`layout.cpp:710-751`) |
| `Mesh::exchange_ghost_zones` does not refresh the $x_1$-wall corners (only the block's per-stage sync does), and a user boundary function that breaks the contract writes wrong corners without an error. | @sec-ch03-cornerrefresh | `Mesh` (`mesh.cpp:389-396`); `refresh` (`meshblock.cpp:932-974`) |
| Selecting `type: cylindrical` runs on unbuilt metric buffers (read from the code; what such a run does is not measured). | @sec-ch03-cylindrical | `Cylindrical` (`coordinate.cpp:599-606`) |
| The centred polynomials have no limiter: across a discontinuity they oscillate, and only the floors stand between an overshoot and a negative density. | @sec-ch04-cp | `interp_cp3` (`interp_simple.hpp:73-75`) |
| Three of the six Riemann solvers cannot return a face pressure, which changes the $x_1$ pressure force on curved grids and in the well-balanced path; the only signal is a hard failure if something asks. | @sec-ch04-riemann | `forward` (`riemann_solver.cpp:39-48`) |
| The Roe solver has no entropy fix: at a sonic point it can admit an expansion shock; no test exercises a transonic rarefaction. | @sec-ch04-roe | `sqrtdl` (`roe_impl.h:39-48`) |
| `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE` is off by default, so every stratified column carries the second-order gap of @eq-ch04-x1masscov-gap; with it on, fewer than three $x_1$ cells fail the run. | @sec-ch04-x1masscov | `x1_mass_covariance` (`hydro_forward.cpp:314-344`) |
| The $x_2$ and $x_3$ reconstructions have no well-balanced treatment; a column hydrostatic in the continuum but not at the discrete fixed point is not at rest. | @sec-ch05-wbx1 | `_hydro_ref_x1` (`hydro_forward.cpp:288-293`) |
| Under the corrected-PE face work (`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT`) every $E+\mathrm{PE}_d$ check, `gravity_work_defect()` included, measures the wrong invariant; there is no form on the cubed sphere, `face-wallc` does not get the scheme, and a block with fewer than three $x_1$ cells books nothing beyond the face form. | @sec-ch06-dwork | `corrected_pe_work` (`hydro_forward.cpp:817-822`); check `d_face_work_pe_check.py` `[C7]` |
| On the `Mesh` path a driver update made after the last stage reaches the ghosts only after the next stage's exchange; a `Mesh` driver with between-step sources is not tested (not measured). | @sec-ch07-exchange | `exchange_ghost_zones` (`meshblock.cpp:545-552`) |
| Only `rk3` is stage-weighted; `rk1`, `rk2` and `rk3s4` run the correction with the full step in every stage. | @sec-ch07-vic-stage | `dt_corr` (`hydro_forward.cpp:929-932`) |
| The VIC closes every column as a reflecting wall whatever the explicit $x_1$ boundary; an open or outflow column still has a closed wall in its implicit solve, accepted silently. | @sec-ch07-vic-closure | `Bnd` (`vic_assemble_full_impl.h:122-126`) |
| The energy and momentum carry of withheld mass runs only where the EOS defines a species enthalpy; with another EOS the limiter withholds mass but the energy is not corrected. | @sec-ch08-carry | `species_enthalpy` (`hydro_forward.cpp:675-677`) |
| The scalar path keeps a scalar non-negative but does not enforce its upper bound; the code comment states the bound as the intent. | @sec-ch08-scalar | `flux_positivity_theta` (`scalar.cpp:158-162`) |
| The EOS floors are absolute values in the deck's units: a deck whose densities are legitimately below $10^{-6}$ is floored in every cell, silently. | @sec-ch08-eoslimiter | `density_floor` (`equation_of_state.cpp:65-72`) |
| A user stage forcing that returns a rate instead of $\Delta t$ times the rate is wrong by a factor $\Delta t$, with no warning; user modules see the stage variables, not the native increment of the same stage. | @sec-ch09-user | `user_stage_forcings` (`meshblock.cpp:689-742`) |
| `coriolis` `type: 123` in two dimensions drops the $x_3$ momentum row when $n_3 = 1$, so the force does work ($\mathbf m\cdot\Delta\mathbf m \ne 0$). | @sec-ch09-coriolis | check `coriolis_check.py` `[C5]` |
| Viscosity and conduction work on Cartesian grids only; `kappa_iso` conducts on $T$, so a resting adiabat drifts; there is no species or tracer diffusion. | @sec-ch09-viscosity | check `viscosity_check.py` |
| Immersed solids are read as fluid by the diffusion module, giving a face heat capacity about 500 times too large; without a `boundary-condition.external` block the one-sided wall rule never fires. | @sec-ch09-wallcoef | `extrapolate_to_wall` (`diffusion.cpp:114-136`) |
| `top-cool`/`bot-heat` use the boundary cell's width for all `depth` cells, so the delivered power is $F$ only on uniform cells; there is no curved-grid volume correction; under an $x_1$ split a `depth` reaching the next block is truncated. | @sec-ch09-heating | check `heating_check.py` `[C2]` |
| Past `max_redo` a moist failure terminates with the rejected state in memory; only the VIC cause restores first. | @sec-ch10-redo | check `redo_check.py` `[C3]` |
| Only the first nucleation reaction producing a condensate sets its parents; the borrowed mass changes phase at fixed $E$, so $T$ moves by the latent heat (size not measured). | @sec-ch10-borrow | check `borrow_check.py` `[C3]` |
| No conserved limiter runs between the driver's kinetics update and `check_redo`, so negative species from kinetics surface as a limiter repair at the next step (chengcli/snapy#256); the update also covers ghosts without an exchange. | @sec-ch10-kinetics | `run_hydro.cpp:191-193` |
| A `custom` no-op does not supply missing ghost data yet still passes the physical-face predicate; `solid` on hydro writes literal ones, not a no-slip or thermodynamic wall; null rectification callbacks are not guarded. | @sec-ch11-custom | `custom_inner` (`bc_func.cpp:7-8`) |
| The public `Mesh::exchange_ghost_zones` only builds sync options and exchanges, so callers cannot assume the block method's $x_1$ refresh; custom callbacks that depend on the full orthogonal shape break the contract. | @sec-ch11-timing | `exchange_ghost_zones` (`meshblock.cpp:545-572`) |
| `pd-run` sets `DEVICE_ID` to the `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` entry while exporting that list unchanged, so a list not starting at 0 names a device the process cannot see (read from the script, not run). | @sec-ch14-launch | `launch_rank` (`pd-run:113-138`) |
| The NetCDF combine globs every `block*` part in the output directory, so parts left from an earlier run with more blocks are joined in (read from the code); `include_ghost_zones` carries a FIXME for non-CCC grids. | @sec-ch14-netcdf | `NetcdfOutput::combine_blocks` (`combine_netcdf.cpp:39-135`); `FIXME` (`netcdf.cpp:72-73`) |
| A restart must be read with the decomposition that wrote it; a single-part restart file is loaded whole by every block, whatever its rank, with no check (read from the code). | @sec-ch14-restart | `load_pt_from_bundle` (`read_restart_file.cpp:154-234`) |

| The implicit time step is stage-weighted only for a three-stage integrator; a direct hydro caller with no published stage gets a one-time warning and the full step. | @sec-ch01-hydro | `dt_corr` (`hydro_forward.cpp:929-944`) |
| The scalar forward divides by the conserved dry density; its behaviour for a zero dry density is not established by the positive-density tests. | @sec-ch01-scalar | `forward` (`scalar.cpp:64-98`) |

| Curved-grid centroid terms do not vanish for an isothermal moving state; exact rest needs zero velocity. | @sec-ch12-flux-covariance | `flux_covariance` (`hydro.cpp:217-259`) |

Each chapter's untested combinations refer to this matrix. | @sec-ch12-matrix | stated in the section |

## Performance and usability {#sec-ch16-usability}

Items where cost, diagnostics, documentation or defaults that surprise a user, with no effect on the results of a correct configuration.

| limit | source | evidence |
|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------|---------------------------|
| The restart writer saves the output counters before `make_outputs` increments them; with the unconditional initial output of `straka`, this is a code-level reason to investigate repeated restart outputs (no overwrite experiment). | @sec-ch01-driver | `make_outputs` (`meshblock.cpp:985-1002`) |
| The accepted `distribute.backend` key does not set the backend; the layout reads the `BACKEND` environment variable instead. | @sec-ch01-options | `from_yaml` (`meshblock_options.cpp:13-88`) |
| Python ctests need `SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH` pointing at the package built from the pin, otherwise they exercise an installed package (CMake warns); the import-path check skips with 125 without it. | @sec-ch01-python | `SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH` (`CMakeLists.txt:350-362`) |
| Temperature-floor positivity and finiteness are not validated in `from_yaml`; the default moist EOS without thermo options fails during reset; ANEOS and shallow water do not satisfy the full moist API. | @sec-ch02-interface | `from_yaml` (`equation_of_state.cpp:33-99`) |
| The programmatic default of `shock` is true but `from_yaml` writes false: construction from Python and from a deck give different schemes unless the key is set. | @sec-ch04-framework | `shock` (`reconstruct.cpp:99-102`) |
| A deck that leaves the reconstruction `type` unset gets first-order donor cell, with no warning. | @sec-ch04-dc | `DonorCellInterp` (`interpolation.cpp:11-12`) |
| Four PLM limiter functions are unreachable, and the slope assumes equal cell widths (on a stretched grid it is not the limited slope of the linear fit). | @sec-ch04-plm | `interp_plm` (`interp_simple.hpp:57-63`) |
| Selecting `ppm` silently gives a first-order scheme. | @sec-ch04-ppm | `interp_ppm` (`interp_simple.hpp:67-69`) |
| The YAML default Riemann solver is `roe`, not the `lmars` the shipped decks use: omitting the key changes the scheme. | @sec-ch04-riemann | `from_yaml` (`riemann_solver.cpp:23-31`) |
| `plume-roe` is a Lax-Friedrichs flux under a name that promises a characteristic solver. | @sec-ch04-shallow | `lax_friedrichs_flux` (`plume_roe.cpp:26-40`) |
| The legacy isentropic wall fill and wall-face copy are dead code; if revived, the fill would conflict with the well-balanced perturbation ghosts. | @sec-ch05-legacy | `_revise_x1inner_lr` (`hydro.cpp:448-453`) |
| `max_redo` is not a YAML key (pyharp's `from_yaml` never reads it), so YAML runs keep the default of 5. | @sec-ch07-rk | `IntegratorImpl` (`pyharp integrator.cpp:33-85`) |
| The time-step bound applies the same `cfl` to every integrator, although `rk3s4` has an SSP coefficient per evaluation of $2/4$ against $1/3$ for `rk3`. | @sec-ch07-rk | `IntegratorImpl::forward` (`pyharp integrator.cpp:101-122`) |
| A VIC failure discards the work of every block for the step (the redo decision is global), and a column that fails at every step size stops the run after `max_redo` retries. | @sec-ch07-vic-reject | `solve_failed` (`implicit_hydro.hpp:96-101`) |
| One switch (`limiter`) turns on the EOS limiter, the tracer limiter, the reconstruction floors and the species clamps together; they cannot be selected independently (a recorded design decision). | @sec-ch08-eoslimiter | `reset_limiter_marks` (`equation_of_state.cpp:352-354`) |
| The vapour column repair throws when a column cannot be repaired (a crash by design), and on a split $x_1$ axis it is a collective gather inside an otherwise local limiter. | @sec-ch08-fixvapor | `repair_column` (`equation_of_state.cpp:274-276`) |
| Forcing modules that are not restricted to interior cells also write into ghost cells (overwritten by the refill), `plume-forcing` is parsed but never installed, and no ctest runs two boundary modules together. | @sec-ch09-framework | `HydroImpl::forward` (`hydro_forward.cpp:754-765`) |
| `traditional` acts only on the cubed sphere (parsed and ignored elsewhere, untested); in `xyz`, `omega1` is $\Omega_z$, `omega2` $\Omega_x$, `omega3` $\Omega_y$. | @sec-ch09-coriolis | `traditional` (`coriolis.cpp:109-142`) |
| `relax-bot-temp` `btemp` defaults to 300 K in the options struct but YAML requires it; `bvx`, `bvy`, `bvz` target $v^1$, $v^2$, $v^3$ ($x_1$ vertical); the velocity drag leaves $E$ untouched, so the removed kinetic energy heats the bottom row. | @sec-ch09-relax | `btemp` (`relax_bot_temp.cpp:80-104`) |
| The saturation-adjustment warm start is discarded whenever kintera is called with another shape or device in between; the cost is not measured. | @sec-ch10-satadj | `warm_start = true` (`kintera thermo_y.cpp:293-310`) |
| Serial callers with several $x_1$ blocks wait at the fix-vapour gather (PR #244); the cross-process gather has not run on CUDA. | @sec-ch10-fixvapor | `fix_vapor_impl` (`fix_vapor_impl.h:9-79`) |
| Casting a block to float32 turns the sedimentation index buffer into floats (PR #258); the MPS path is untested; the default gas constants describe an H2 background. | @sec-ch10-sed | `SedVelImpl::forward` (`sed_vel.cpp:34-71`) |
| The fixed-temperature boundary names are whitelisted but no built-in registration exists, so they do not provide a thermal boundary; the comment calling outflow zero-gradient is stale. | @sec-ch11-registry | `is_wall_boundary` (`meshblock_options.cpp:218-271`) |
| Unknown strings silently enable the `SNAP_*` environment switches, and cross-rank consistency of the environment is the launcher's responsibility. | @sec-ch12-environment | check `configuration_check.py` |
| `pd-run` exports `BLOCKS_PER_PROCESS`, which nothing under `src/` reads; it starts every process on the local host (no multi-node mode). | @sec-ch14-launch | `launch_rank` (`pd-run:113-138`) |
| A caller that steps the local blocks one by one waits 5 minutes at the first board and stops, or forever at the sync rendezvous; the bound of 32 local blocks for the base tag is implied, not checked. | @sec-ch14-msgmatch | `take_x1_anchor` (`layout.cpp:879-970`); `make_comm_tag` (`layout.hpp:161-170`) |
| Signals are read only in `check_redo`: a rank that never reaches it hangs the others; every collective blocks on the host, costing a device-to-host copy on GPU. | @sec-ch14-collectives | `CheckSignalFlags` (`signal_handler.cpp:64-86`) |
| A step on a small 2-D moist grid costs 1.54 times more on 2.11.2 than on 2.10.9 (issue #291, open: 3005 against 2061 kernels, 33 against 7 `.item()` per step; not re-measured); a driver asking for CUDA on a machine without it runs on the CPU silently. | @sec-ch14-gpu | chengcli/snapy#291; `torch::cuda::is_available` (`run_hydro.cpp:39-47`) |
| The default float output hides relative changes below about $10^{-7}$; conservation is read from the double-precision cycle line. | @sec-ch14-netcdf | `nc_dbl` (`netcdf.cpp:191-195`) |
| A resumed run rewrites its last outputs, including its source restart file, and the restart index does not advance (chengcli/snapy#277, open); run-to-date meters are not carried across a restart. | @sec-ch14-restart | chengcli/snapy#277; `gravity_work_fix` (`hydro.hpp:186-190`) |
| An output interval shorter than the step fires every step until the schedule catches up; the statistics sample accepted states only. | @sec-ch14-schedule | `MeshBlockImpl::make_outputs` (`meshblock.cpp:985-1002`) |
| `pd-combine` globs every `*.out*.nc` in the directory, needs NCO, deletes its inputs by default, and does not join per-block files. | @sec-ch14-tools | `ParseOutputFields` (`pd_combine.py:43-59`) |

## Conservation budgets and diagnostics (not in the book yet) {#sec-ch16-ch13}

The conservation chapter is on draft PR #38 (head `c2d1ea20df5c72aa00efbf60c3bd664f887768f3`), so its sections cannot be cross-referenced yet; they are named by title. The items join the tables above, with references, when it merges.

| limit | class | section (draft) | evidence |
|--------------------------------------------------|------------|----------------|----------------------|
| The `div` output diagnostic uses two-cell face means, not the reconstructed states, so it is not the divergence the scheme saw. | restricted | Output diagnostics | `interp_to_face` (`load_diag_output_data.cpp:22-45`) |
| No registered test checks `mass0=` over a full example run; the only such check is a script no CMake rule calls, comparing first and last samples. | restricted | Regression of the cycle line | `check_mass` (`run_example_mass_check.py:133-144`) |
| The cycle line is a record, not a check: a drift in `mass0=` is visible only to a reader or a test that parses the log. | usability | Cycle line | `print_cycle_info` (`run_hydro.cpp:161-164`) |
| `limcut` measures the $x_1$ flux only; a limiter acting in $x_2$ or $x_3$ shows only in `thetamin` and `thetasevere`. | usability | Limiter meters | `_lim_cut` (`hydro_forward.cpp:690-705`) |
| The VIC clamp meter is a run maximum: it says that a clamp bound somewhere at some time, not when or where. | usability | VIC clamp meter | `vicclamp` (`meshblock.cpp:1108`) |
| The log names redo causes but not the cells or rank that raised them; only a VIC refusal prints its column. | usability | Redo causes in the log | `reduce_redo_flags` (`meshblock.cpp:1288-1300`) |

- $x_1$ seams between blocks (concurrency and 5-minute anchor wait, the 16-block limit, one-sided radial-exact slopes at block edges, seam-flux averaging, the serial anchor relay): pending #303; current text in @sec-ch03-x1seams, @sec-ch04-seam, @sec-ch05-seam.
